q: What ancient Sanskrit phrase on the noticeboard means 'food gives life to living beings'?
What are the major nutrient classes required by the human body?
a: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Vitamins, Minerals, Dietary Fiber (Roughage), and Water.

q: Explain the ancient Indian dietary maxim 'Hitabhuk, Ritabhuk, Mitabhuk'.
a: It advocates eating wholesome food (Hitabhuk), eating seasonal food (Ritabhuk), and eating in measured moderation (Mitabhuk).

q: What are the nutritional differences observed when comparing potato wafers with roasted chana?
a: Potato wafers contain high fat and sodium with low protein/fiber (junk food), while roasted chana supplies rich proteins, complex carbohydrates, dietary fiber, and minerals (wholesome food).

q: Name four native Indian millets highlighted as nutrient-dense superfoods.
a: Jowar (Sorghum), Bajra (Pearl Millet), Ragi (Finger Millet), and Sanwa (Barnyard Millet).

q: Why is dietary fiber (roughage) essential in our daily diet even though it yields no direct calories?
a: Roughage adds necessary bulk to digested food, promotes smooth intestinal motility, prevents constipation, and supports healthy gut microbiota.
